newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France seeks China cargo partners.
newsitem.headline: Air France seeks China cargo partners.

text.p: Air France wants to establish a joint-venture cargo operation in China as part of an effort to widen its penetration of the Asian market.

The French flag carrier's director general for cargo, Sten Grotenfelt, told Reuters in an interview that talks were already in progress with Air China "more on a joint-venture basis and not on a strong alliance basis" but declined to offer This would be more than just a commercial alliance such as the capacity sharing arrangement it currently has with China Eastern on its Shanghai services.

"China is certainly an interesting local market and also well positioned to distribute from," he added. The creation of a cargo hub in China could serve both Chinese and other Asian areas on links with Europe. Air France currently operates four weekly services Paris-Beijing and once weekly Paris-Shanghai.

"We are interested in establishing ourselves more in the Asian region to develop business there because, of course, that's the fastest growing area." he said. "I think we can do more in that part of the world."
Air France's present cargo links in Asia include pooling deals with Thai International, Japan Airlines and Singapore Airlines.

Grotenfelt said any such agreement would be part of a quest for "more alliances and co-operation" in the cargo area, but added it was not the result of a changed management culture within the French carrier.

He added that the recently-signed commercial agreement with U.S. carriers Continental Airlines and Delta Airlines, did not include "a more dedicated cargo operation but we will certainly take up that issue in due course."
